notes: §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR10: "Class-name-1 can be referenced only in a class condition"; each numeric literal is the ordinal of a character in the native set, each character of a nonnumeric literal is a member, and a THROUGH pair adds the contiguous native characters "in either ascending or descending sequence". SpecialNamesBinder#SwitchBindClass builds the member set at 85 through LiteralPhraseOperand (ordinal n is code unit n-1 of the 65,536-character native set) and OneCharacterOperands, swapping a descending pair; ConditionBinder#BindUserWordClassCondition is the only reader and CobolClass#IsInClass tests each character; VersionConformancePass#VisitClassDefinitionClause refuses the 2002 IN alphabet-name and FOR phrases at 85 (kb/Work PB5172, landed: the prior PARTIAL). Probes at --std 85: d) SPACE, QUOTE, ZERO, ALL "XY", HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VALUE THRU " " ("!" outside), repeated characters, a group operand, ordinal 66 THRU "A" and ALL "A" THRU "C" all answer right, a numeric operand is COBOL6916; b) ordinal 0, 65537 and 70000, +66, 66.0, "AB" THRU "C", a symbolic-character (SR5), a second CLASS C1 and an empty CLASS are refused, 65536 is admitted; c) IN AL, FOR ALPHANUMERIC, N"A", X"41" COBOL0900; the reference bar holds (MOVE, DISPLAY and a relation operand are refused, though as COBOL1639 'not defined' at every edition, a misleading wording with no kb/Work note found). a), e) and f) do not reach a SPECIAL-NAMES rule. The witness runs six 1985-format classes (multi-character, THRU both ways, ordinals). History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5172 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-11.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-11-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: 'Class-name-1 can be referenced only in a class condition'; literal values are ordinals or characters 'within the native character set'. §2023:12.3.7.4 GR12 keeps the exclusive set, ordinal/character meaning, multi-character literals and THROUGH in either order, but drops the class-condition-only restriction (§2023:13.18.11.4 GR1 references a class-name in the data-division CLASS clause) and adds 'or, when the IN phrase is specified, within the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4' (§2023:12.3.7.3 SR17 also adds the NATIONAL phrase).
